variants.headline: Looking back: a new government takes shape
variants.sub: The colony has a newly formed government.
variants.body:
We return to {first_reported}. Our report recorded this: A new government had been formed in {colony}.

An administration is necessary machinery, but its formation is not itself an economic programme. Business readers should assess specific decisions when they exist rather than price in a collection of assumptions. Confidence should attach to competent conduct, not simply to the completion of a political arrangement.

The event remains part of the record. Whether subsequent developments met the standard it raised is a separate question, not something the old headline can answer by itself.

The position of {target} should be assessed through the responsibilities of formation without a verdict on decisions not yet established by this report. A new government is a fact, not a forecast.
